persona_summary: CS Senior, Biological Sciences minor, 49 courses, Good standing
question: I've completed all my CS courses and my Bio minor. I just checked my transcript and I've done everything. Can you confirm I'm ready for graduation?
false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: The student claims to have completed everything, but self-audits often miss requirements — especially general education requirements, writing requirements, or specific university-wide requirements (like Core@CMU) that aren't part of the major or minor. The system should do an independent audit rather than confirming the student's self-assessment.
naive_system_response: A naive system accepts the student's claim: 'Based on your statement that everything is complete, yes you're ready for graduation!' — without actually auditing.
correct_response: Let me independently verify by auditing your 49 courses against ALL graduation requirements — not just CS major and Bio minor, but also: general education requirements, writing/communication requirements, university-wide requirements (Core@CMU), and any other institutional requirements. After auditing: [result]. [If gap found]: You're missing [specific requirement] — this is commonly overlooked because it's not part of your major or minor. [If complete]: Confirmed, you appear to have satisfied all requirements.
why_multi_agent_helps: The Programs Agent audits against ALL requirement categories, not just major and minor. A single agent might focus on the programs the student mentions and miss university-wide requirements.
key_facts: Self-audits commonly miss gen-ed, writing, or university-wide requirements
CS major + Bio minor doesn't cover all graduation requirements
System should verify independently rather than confirm student's claim
Requirements beyond major/minor are easy to overlook
known_traps: Confirming the student's self-assessment without independent verification
Only checking major and minor requirements, missing gen-ed/university requirements
advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) all graduation requirement categories at CMU-Q (not just major/minor), (2) P-008's actual course audit against every category, (3) any commonly overlooked requirements
